Dear Sir / Madam, 
Sub: Submission of Annual Report of the Company for the Financial Year 2025-26 
along with the Notice of the 41st Annual General Meeting. 
In compliance with Regulation 30 and 34 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, please find attached herewith the 
Annual Report of the Company for the Financial Year 2025-26 including the Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and the Notice of the 41st Annual 
General Meeting (“AGM”), which has been sent through electronic mode to the 
members on September 02, 2026. The 41st Annual General Meeting of the Company is 
scheduled to be held on Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 04:00 P.M. IST through Video 
Conferencing (“VC”)/ Other Audio Visual Means (“OAVM”) without the physical 
presence of the Members at a common venue.  
Please be informed that the Company is providing e-voting facility to its shareholders 
in respect of resolutions to be passed at the AGM. The Company has engaged the 
services of National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) as the authorized agency 
to provide remote e-voting facility.  
The remote e-Voting facility will be available during the following period: 
Commencement of e-Voting 
Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 9.00 A.M. IST  
End of e-Voting
Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 5.00 P.M. IST 
 
During this period, Members holding shares either in physical form or in 
dematerialized form as on Thursday, September 17, 2026 ('Cut-Off date') may cast 
their vote by remote e-Voting. The detailed instructions with respect to voting have 
been mentioned in the Notice of AGM. 
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India (‘MCA’), vide its Circular No. 
20/2020 dated May 5, 2020, and subsequent circulars issued from time to time, the 
latest being General Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 22, 2025, along with other 
relevant circulars in this regard (hereinafter collectively referred to as the ‘MCA 
Circulars’), has permitted the conduct of Annual General Meetings (‘AGMs’) through 

 
 
Video Conferencing (‘VC’) / Other Audio-Visual Means (‘OAVM’) facility. 
Accordingly, in compliance with the MCA Circulars, the applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’), the AGM of the 
Company is being conducted through VC/OAVM facility, without the physical 
presence of the Members at a common venue. 
Accordingly, the Annual Report together with the Notice of the AGM has been 
dispatched only by electronic mode to those Shareholders whose email addresses are 
registered with the Company/ MUFG Intime India Private Limited (Formerly known 
as  Link Intime India Private Limited) - Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)/ 
Depository Participant(s) / Depositories. 
A letter providing the web-link, including the exact path and QR code, where the 
Annual Report for the Financial Year 2025-26 is available, is being sent to those 
members whose e-mail address is not registered with the Company/ MUFG Intime 
India Private Limited (Formerly known as Link Intime India Private Limited) - 
Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)/ Depository Participant(s) / Depositories. 
The Annual Report together with the Notice of the AGM can also be accessed from 
the websites of the Company at www.welspunliving.com, National Securities 
Depository Limited (NSDL) at www.evoting.nsdl.com, Stock Exchanges where the 
shares of the Company are listed i.e. BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited at www.bseindia.com and www.nseindia.com, respectively.

10. Deduction of Tax
 
As you are aware that the Board of Directors of the 
Company, at its meeting held on May 15, 2026, have 
recommended a dividend at the rate of 10% equity per 
share i.e. H 0.10/- per Equity Share of face value Re. 1/- 
each fully paid-up for the Financial Year ended March 
31, 2026.
 
The dividend, as recommended by the Board, if 
approved at the ensuing annual general meeting, 
will be paid to the equity shareholders holding equity 
shares of the Company as at the record date i.e. Friday, 
July 10, 2026.
 
In accordance with the provisions of the Income-tax 
Act, 2025 (as amended by Finance Act, 2026) (‘the 
Act’), dividend paid or distributed by a Company, shall 
be taxable at the hands of shareholders. Accordingly, 
the Company is required to deduct tax at source from 
dividend paid to the shareholders, if approved at the 
Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Company.
 
This communication provides a brief of the applicable 
Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) provisions under the Act 
for Resident and Non-Resident shareholder categories.
I. 
For Resident Shareholders:
 
Tax is required to be deducted at source under Section 
393(1) [Table Sr. No. 7] read with Section 393(4) [Table 
Sr. No. 10] of the Act, at the rate of 10% on the amount 
of dividend where shareholders have registered their 
valid Permanent Account Number (PAN). In case, 
shareholders do not have PAN / have not registered 
their valid PAN details in their account, TDS at the rate 
of 20% shall be deducted under Section 397(2) of 
the Act.
a. 
Resident Individuals:
 
No tax shall be deducted on the dividend payable to 
resident individuals if:
 
i. 
Total dividend amount to be received by them 
during the Financial Year (FY) 2026-27 does not 
exceed H 10,000/; or
 
ii. 
The shareholder provides Form 121, provided 
that all the required eligibility conditions are met. 
Please note that all fields are mandatory to be 
filled up and Company may at its sole discretion 
reject the form if it does not fulfil the requirement 
of law. Format of Form 121 is enclosed herewith 
as Annexure-1.
 
iii. 
Exemption certificate, if any, issued by the 
Income-tax Department.
b. 
Resident Non-Individuals:
 
No tax shall be deducted on the dividend payable to the 
following resident non-individuals where they provide 
prescribed details and documents as per the format 
attached in Annexure-2.
 
i. 
Insurance Companies: Self declaration that 
it qualifies as ‘Insurer’ as per section 2(7A) of 
the Insurance Act, 1938 and has full beneficial 
interest with respect to the ordinary shares owned 
by it along with self-attested copy of PAN card 
and certificate of registration with Insurance 
Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA)/ 
LIC/ GIC.

ii. 
Mutual Funds: Self-declaration that it is registered 
with SEBI and is specified under Schedule VII 
[Table: Sl. No. 20 or 21] of the Act along with 
self-attested copy of PAN card and certificate of 
registration with SEBI.
 
iii. 
Alternative Investment Fund (AIF):  Self-
declaration that its income is exempt under 
Section 11 - Schedule V [Table Sr. No. 1] of the 
Act, and they are registered with SEBI as Category 
I or Category II AIF along with self-attested copy 
of the PAN card and certificate of AIF registration 
with SEBI.
 
iv. 
New Pension System (NPS) Trust:  Self-
declaration that it qualifies as NPS trust and 
income is eligible for exemption under section 
11-Schedule VII [Table Sr. No. 41] of the Act and 
being regulated by the provisions of the Indian 
Trusts Act, 1882 along with self-attested copy of 
the PAN card.
 
v. 
Other Non-Individual shareholders:  Self-
attested copy of documentary evidence 
supporting the exemption along with self-attested 
copy of PAN card.
II. 
For Non-resident Shareholders:
a. 
Taxes are required to be withheld in accordance with 
the provisions of Section 393(2) [Table Sr. No. 17 and 
15] of the Act as per the rates as applicable. As per the 
relevant provisions of the Act, the withholding tax shall 
be at the rate of 20% (plus applicable surcharge and 
cess) on the amount of dividend payable to them. In 
case, non-resident shareholders provide a certificate 
issued under Section 395 of the Act, for lower/ 
Nil withholding of taxes, rate specified in the said 
certificate shall be considered, on submission of self-
attested copy of the same.
b. 
Further, as per Section 159 of the Act, the non-resident 
shareholder has the option to be governed by the 
provisions of the Double Tax Avoidance Treaty (DTAA) 
between India and the country of tax residence of the 
shareholder, if they are more beneficial to them. For this 
purpose, i.e., to avail Tax Treaty benefit, the non-resident 
shareholders are required to provide the following:
 
i. 
Self-attested copy of the PAN card allotted by 
the Indian Income Tax authorities.  In case, PAN 
is not available, the non-resident shareholder 
shall furnish (a) name, (b) email id, (c) contact 
number, (d) address in residency country, 
(e) Tax Identification Number of the residency 
country, format attached herewith as Annexure 3.
 
ii. 
Self-attested copy of Tax Residency Certificate 
(TRC) (for financial year April 1, 2026 to March 
31, 2027) obtained from the tax authorities of the 
country of which the shareholder is a resident.
 
iii. 
Copy of E-filed Form 41 (filed electronically on 
the Indian Income Tax web portal pursuant to 
Notification no. 03/2022 dated July 16, 2022) 
valid for the period April 2026 to March 2027.
 
iv. 
Self-declaration by shareholder of meeting treaty 
eligibility requirement and satisfying beneficial 
ownership requirement. (For the FY April 1, 2026 
to March 31, 2027), format attached herewith as 
Annexure 3.
 
v. 
In case of Foreign Institutional Investors and 
Foreign Portfolio Investors, copy of SEBI 
registration certificate.
 
vi. 
In case of a shareholder being tax resident of 
a country, with which India has a Double Tax 
Avoidance Agreement (‘DTAA’) and the said DTAA 
has a Limitation of Benefits Article, please furnish 
the letter issued by the competent authority or 
any other declaration/ evidence demonstrating 
the non-applicability of said Limitation of Relief 
under the relevant DTAA.
 
It is recommended that shareholders should 
independently satisfy their eligibility to claim DTAA 
benefit including meeting of all conditions laid down 
by DTAA.
 
Kindly note that the Company is not obligated to apply 
beneficial DTAA rates at the time of tax deduction 
/ withholding on dividend amounts. Application 
of beneficial rate as per DTAA for the purpose of 
withholding taxes shall depend upon completeness and 
satisfactory review by the Company of the documents 
submitted by the non-resident shareholder.
III. Lower withholding as per Certificate under 
Section 395:
 
In case, shareholders (resident or non-resident) 
provide certificate under Section 395 of the Act, for

ITEM NO. 7 and 8 – Material Related Party 
Transaction(s) with Welspun Global Brands

In terms of Regulation 23 of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing 
Regulations, 2015”), as amended, material related 
party transactions (“RPT”) require prior approval of the 
shareholders through ordinary resolutions, even if such 
transactions are in the ordinary course of business of the 
Company and at an arm’s length basis.
Pursuant to Regulation 23 read with Schedule XII of 
the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, as amended, RPT 
is considered material if the transaction(s), whether 
entered into individually or taken together with previous 
transactions during a financial year, exceeds 10% of the 
annual consolidated turnover of the Company as per its last 
audited financial statements, where the annual consolidated 
turnover of the Company is up to H 20,000 crore. Accordingly, 
the materiality threshold for seeking shareholders’ approval 
for related party transactions of the Company is H 940 crore.
Further, as per Regulation 2(1)(zc) of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, 2015, the definition of RPT includes a 
transaction involving a transfer of resources, services or 
obligations between a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries 
on one hand and a related party of the listed entity or any of 
its subsidiaries on the other hand, regardless of whether a 
price is charged or not.
Accordingly, the Company is seeking the approval of the 
Members for the transactions proposed under Item Nos. 7 
and 8 of the accompanying Notice, as set out below.
Background, details and benefits of the transactions
Welspun Living Limited (“Company” or “WLL”) is a publicly 
listed company whose equity shares are listed and traded 
on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India 
Limited. The Company and its subsidiaries and associates 
(collectively, the “Welspun Living Group”) are engaged in 
the manufacture, marketing and sale of towels, rugs, bed 
sheets and other home textile products across various 
geographies and customer segments.
The Welspun Living Group operates through an integrated 
business model under which WLL and other entities within 
the group undertake manufacturing activities, while 
Welspun Global Brands Limited (“WGBL”), a subsidiary 
of the Company, primarily undertakes marketing, brand 
management and distribution activities. WGBL markets and 
distributes products manufactured by the Welspun Living 
Group across international markets and services customers 
across retail, institutional and e-commerce segments.
Welspun USA Inc. (“WUSA”), a step-down subsidiary of 
the Company and a subsidiary of WGBL, operates as the 
Welspun Living Group’s business and distribution platform 
in the United States, which is one of its single largest 
export markets. WUSA provides six principal categories of 
services: (i) product sales facilitation, (ii) market analytics, 
(iii) design and product development support, (iv) supply-
chain management, (v) warehousing and (vi) customer 
relationship management. Through these activities, WUSA 
supports the Welspun Living Group’s relationships with 
customers in the United States and facilitates the distribution 
of products manufactured and/or marketed by the group.

1 
Sale of Goods by Welspun Global Brands Limited
The proposed transactions between WGBL and WUSA form part of 
the established arrangements supporting the Welspun Living Group’s 
business in the United States.
WUSA is the Welspun Living Group’s established US business and 
distribution platform and supports relationships with major US retailers, 
including Walmart, Costco, Target and Amazon.
WUSA provides six principal categories of services: (i) product sales 
facilitation, (ii) market analytics, (iii) design and product development 
support, (iv) supply-chain management, (v) warehousing and (vi) 
customer relationship management. These capabilities provide local 
market access and customer-facing infrastructure while complementing 
WGBL’s centralised marketing, brand management and distribution 
functions.
The proposed transactions enable the Welspun Living Group to leverage 
WUSA’s local capabilities and infrastructure without duplicating 
functions within WGBL, while facilitating the movement of products, 
customer servicing and supply-chain coordination in the US market.
Accordingly, the proposed transactions support WGBL’s US distribution 
and customer servicing activities, optimise the use of existing Welspun 
Living Group infrastructure and resources, and facilitate the Welspun 
Living Group’s ability to service its US customer base efficiently. 
The transactions are in the ordinary course of business and will be 
undertaken on an arm’s length basis.

Looking back from the day we entered the 40th year of 
running a successful business, we see that Welspun 
hasn’t grown alone. We believe that sustainable value 
can be created only through shared growth. And, our 
growth has been inseparable from the lives of the 
communities living around us. 
Our 24,000-strong workforce ensuring global-best 
systems in environmental management, sustainable 
practices and efficient governance toil hard for the 
welfare of people living beyond the economic shadow 
lines. Welspun holds regular training camps to make 
the working-age population living around our facilities 
employable through skill development and spread of 
education and awareness. 
Our push for a barrier-free workplace, ensuring 
equitable distribution of opportunity, has pushed us to 
the top league of Indian corporates with women making

planet is our biggest stakeholder. We are guided by this 
philosophy at every step which eventually led us to rank 
first globally in the DJSI S&P Corporate Sustainability 
Assessment (CSA) 2025.
Our commitment to the planet reflects in the way we 
run a water-intensive industry. Our advanced water 
harvesting system reduces water consumption, 
recycles the precious resource and reuses it for 
production. We have laid out a green power roadmap 
to the Net Zero emissions target by 2040. Our 
decarbonisation initiatives are deeply seeded in 
our operations. 
While building for the future, our innovative mindset 
plays a crucial role. Welspun constantly upgrades itself 
by adopting advanced technologies. Our blockchain-
based system, Wel-Trak® 2.0, helps in traceability from 
farm to fabric. It gives complete transparency to our 
consumers shoring up our sustainability initiatives. 
We set new benchmarks at every step towards a 
greener future, promising success for everyone.

strategic conviction.
While the external environment impacted our

reaffirmed the strength of the foundations 
we have built over the last four decades. 
Throughout the year, we remained focused

Navigating the tariff headwinds
The sharp escalation in US tariff was the defining event 
of the year, and its impact was severe. About 59% of 
our revenue is US-facing. These partnerships have 
been built over decades and are central to our long-
term success. While protecting them came at a cost in 
the short term, but preserving trust and market position 
was the right strategic decision and we are convinced 
of that today.
Periods of disruptions often accelerate structural 
change. During the year, India strengthened its 
position as a preferred sourcing destination through 
progress on trade agreements with major economies, 
including the European Union and the United Kingdom 
as well as advancement of the India-US Bilateral 
Trade Agreement. Meaningful movement across 
three of our most important export markets within a 
relatively short period has the potential to enhance 
India’s competitiveness and support long term growth 
prospects of the textile industry.
The EU and UK combined represent a home textile 
market worth over $30 billion. Combined with the 
ongoing diversification of global supply chains away 
from concentrated sourcing geographies, these 
agreements create a durable competitive advantage 
for India. What was once a cyclical opportunity is 
increasingly becoming a structural one.
Our efforts to diversify geographically also proved 
valuable during the year. Non-US revenues increased 
to 41% of total revenues, reflecting deliberate 
investments made over several years to broaden our 
market presence and reduce concentration risk. This 
diversification provided important resilience at a time 
when it was needed most.
Balance sheet strength as a 
strategic advantage
In a year marked by revenue pressure and volatility, 
financial discipline emerged as one of our greatest 
strengths. While the operating environment was 
challenging, our focus on cash generation, working 
capital efficiency and prudent capital allocation 
enabled us to strengthen the balance sheet and 
enhance financial flexibility. 
The outcomes were not incidental. They were the 
result of deliberate choices: maintaining capital 
discipline, optimising inventory, improving receivables 
management and directing resources towards the 
highest-value opportunities. In uncertain times, a 
strong balance sheet is more than a financial metric— 
it is a strategic advantage.
Our confidence in the long-term prospects of the 
business was also reflected in our capital allocation 
decisions. During the year, the Board approved a ₹252 
crore share buyback and a 10% dividend, underscoring 
our commitment to creating shareholder value while 
continuing to invest in future growth.
As the year progressed, early signs of recovery began 
to emerge. In Q4 FY26, we delivered healthy sequential 
revenue growth and improvements in EBITDA margins. 
While there is more work ahead, the trajectory of the 
business is encouraging and reinforces our confidence 
in the path forward.

Building a consumer-led growth 
engine
For several years, we have articulated our ambition 
to become the FMCG of textiles—a company where 
brands, innovation and consumer relationships create 
enduring value alongside manufacturing excellence. 
FY26 marked an important step in that journey.
While our export business navigated significant tariff-
related disruption, our consumer-facing businesses 
demonstrated resilience and continued to grow. 
Domestic consumer revenues increased 9% to ₹657 
crore, while our branded and consumer portfolio 
contributed around one-fifth of the total revenue share. 
More importantly, these businesses provided stability 
in a year marked by external volatility, validating our 
strategy of building stronger consumer connections 
and diversified growth engines.
Our vision of 'Har Ghar Se Har Dil Tak Welspun' 
(From Every Home to Every Heart Welspun) gained 
meaningful traction during the year. The progress 
we witnessed was driven not merely by distribution 
expansion, but by increasing consumer preference, 
brand trust and product relevance.
Across global markets, our brand portfolio continued 
to strengthen their presence. Christy reinforced its 
position as a premium heritage brand while expanding 
into US through premium retailers and e-commerce 
and strengthening its presence across SEA and ANZ. 
Welhome scaled its footprint with strong traction across 
North America and expansion underway in UK and key 
Asian markets. We also accelerated our growth in the 
pillows segment, supported by higher utilisation at our 
Ohio facility and the commencement of operations at 
our Nevada facility, strengthening our manufacturing 
platform in the United States.
Our investment in US pillow manufacturing is not a 
response to tariffs alone. It represents a strategic entry 
into one of the fastest-growing categories within home 
textiles and reflects our broader approach of building 
growth platforms closer to the consumer. As we look 
ahead, brands, innovation and consumer engagement 
will increasingly complement manufacturing scale as 
key drivers of value creation.
Sustainability as a competitive 
moat
Sustainability is no longer just a responsibility; it 
is increasingly becoming a source of competitive 
advantage. In FY26, Welspun Living ranked #1 globally 
in ESG S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment in 
Textiles, Apparels & Luxury goods category (as on 
11th Dec 2025). This reflects a sustained journey of 
improvement, with our score rising from 59 in FY23 to 
90 in FY26.
Our commitment to sustainability is closely linked to 
innovation. Our portfolio of over 50 patents, including 
products such as HygroCotton®, GX Pillow® and  
Wel-Trak®, contributed 22% of revenues during the 
year, demonstrating how responsible innovation can 
create meaningful business value.
As sustainability becomes a key consideration 
in sourcing decisions for global retailers, our 
leadership position strengthens customer trust, 
enhances differentiation and reinforces our long-
term competitiveness.
Our people
Throughout FY26, our people remained the 
foundation of our resilience and progress. While many 
organisations responded to uncertainty by reducing 
workforce capacity, we chose to preserve the talent, 
capabilities and institutional knowledge that have been 
built over decades. We believe long-term success 
is driven not only by financial capital, but also by 
human capital.
We earned the Great Place to Work® certification for 
the second consecutive year, reflecting our continued 
focus on building a culture of trust, growth and 
inclusion. Women now constitute more than 35% of our 
workforce, among the highest representation levels in 
the industry.
Our SPUN initiative continued to create meaningful 
impact by transforming factory waste into livelihood 
opportunities for rural women artisans, demonstrating 
how sustainability and social inclusion can go hand 
in hand.

The road ahead
We enter FY27 with a stronger balance sheet, a more 
diversified business model, growing brands, industry-
leading sustainability credentials and a clear strategic 
direction. While FY26 tested our resilience, it also 
reinforced the strengths that position us for  
long-term growth. Our aspiration of building a 
₹15,000 crore revenue enterprise in medium-term 
remains firmly intact.
Our priorities are clear: deepen our branded and 
consumer businesses, capitalise on the opportunities 
emerging from new trade agreements, scale our 
US manufacturing presence in pillows and adjacent 
categories, and continue investing in innovation, 
technology and design to strengthen differentiation.
India's domestic economy remains a source of strength, 
while the ongoing diversification of global sourcing 
continues to create opportunities for competitive and 
reliable suppliers. Combined with the trade frameworks 
now taking shape across key export markets, these 
trends provide a strong runway for future growth.
I am grateful to our Board for their guidance, our 
leadership team for their steadfast execution, our 
Welspunites for their passion and commitment, our 
customers for their trust, and our shareholders for 
their continued confidence. We look ahead with 
optimism, confidence and a clear sense of purpose. 
We remain committed to creating enduring value for all 
stakeholders and shaping the future of home textiles 
from India to the world.

Resilient through change. 
Dear Stakeholders,
We have left behind a year that marked a defining 
phase in the evolution of global trade. Heightened tariff 
volatility, geopolitical tensions, persistent inflationary 
pressures, and muted discretionary demand combined 
to create one of the most challenging operating 
environments in recent years. Welspun Living lived 
through this period of uncertainty with steadfast 
commitment to protecting what it treasures the most: 
customers, people, capabilities and long-term vision.
The situation demanded agility and disciplined 
execution. India demonstrated remarkable resilience, 
strengthening its position as a preferred sourcing 
destination for global corporations. As trade 
agreements with major consumption markets such as 
the US, the UK, the EU, Japan and Australia continue to 
progress and deepen economic partnerships, they are 
expected to create new opportunities beyond a cyclical 
recovery. These evolving trade relationships have the 
potential to reinforce India's long-term competitiveness, 
positioning the country and companies with strong 
resolve, such as Welspun Living, to thrive in a rapidly 
evolving global landscape.
Our resolve paid off with the fourth quarter of FY26 
giving out early signs of recovery and improving 
momentum. Revenues grew 7.7% sequentially, while 
EBITDA margins improved sharply to 10.8%, expanding 
313 basis points from the preceding quarter. Free 
cash flows for FY26 increased 8.5 times to ₹956 crore, 
alongside a 52% reduction in net debt, reinforcing the 
resilience of our operating model as we entered FY27 
with greater confidence.
Positioned for

Defying disruptive forces with 
conviction
In FY26, our consolidated revenues stood at ₹9,468 
crore, marking the fifth straight year of over $1 billion 
revenue. Despite the external disruptions, we chose 
not to digress from our focus on bolstering the core of 
the business and enhancing our long-term competitive 
edge. Throughout the year, we took deliberate 
actions to preserve customer trust and deepen global 
partnerships, ensuring continuity, reliability and service 
excellence even amid volatile tariffs.
The US continues to remain a core and strategic market 
for us, underpinned by India’s leadership position with 
nearly 45% share in cotton terry towels and around 60% 
share in cotton bed sheets. At the same time, we have 
made steady progress on our regional diversification, 
building a more balanced global portfolio. Non-US 
markets made up around 41% of our revenues in 
FY26, with growing presence across Europe, the UK, 
GCC, Japan, ANZ, and other regions. This expanding 
footprint not only reduces concentration risk but also 
positions us well to capitalise on the next phase of 
global sourcing realignment enabled by FTAs and 
supply chain shifts.
Our focus on operational discipline also strengthened 
the balance sheet considerably. Through tighter 
working capital management and disciplined capital 
allocation, we generated robust free cash flows and 
significantly reduced net debt during the year—
enhancing financial resilience and creating greater 
flexibility for future investments.
A wider portfolio for evolving 
expectations
Our strategic focus remains firmly on building a 
diversified, consumer-led, and innovation-driven 
portfolio for long-term value creation. Our branded 
business has emerged as a strong growth driver, 
contributing about 19.3% of revenues, with clear 
acceleration through the year. Globally, Christy 
delivered a 15% growth, strengthening its premium 
positioning across key markets, while our home-grown 
brand Welhome scaled to $19.4 million, gaining traction 
across North America and expanding into markets such 
as Japan, the UK, China and Taiwan. Our hospitality 
business continues to scale steadily, deepening 
partnerships with leading global hotel chains and 
reinforcing our positioning while bridging institutional 
scale with consumer visibility. In Q4, this momentum 
was further reflected in the domestic business, 
which grew around 29% YoY, supported by continued 
premiumisation and sharper channel execution.
Alongside brands, we are consciously expanding into 
higher-value categories and differentiated segments. 
The sleep solutions ecosystem remains a high-
conviction growth area, with our pillow business nearly 
doubling from $15 million to $27.5 million, supported 
by strong ramp-up of our Ohio facility reaching 60% 
utilisation and the commencement of commercial 
production at our Nevada greenfield facility on 
31 March 2026. 
In a parallel, categories such as utility bedding, fashion 
bedding, and design-led terry, including fashion 
towels, are gaining traction, supporting improved 
realisations and a structurally stronger product mix. 
These segments, anchored in design, functionality, 
and innovation, are enabling us to move up the value 
chain and strengthen our positioning in higher-
margin offerings.
Innovation remains deeply embedded in our DNA 
and continues to drive this transformation. With an 
IP portfolio of 50 patents and innovation contributing 
around 22% of revenues, we continue to build 
a differentiated product ecosystem backed by 
proprietary technologies such as HygroCotton®, GX 
Pillow®, and Wel-Trak®. This strong innovation platform 
not only supports premiumisation but also enhances 
customer stickiness, enabling us to sustain long-term 
competitive advantage in an evolving global market.

to be freshwater positive and commissioned a recycling 
plant at Anjar, to secure waste traceability and make 
greater reuse of industrial wastes in sync with our circular 
economy objective.

ESG assessments and industry benchmarks. During 
FY26, Welspun Living was recognised among India's 
Most Sustainable Companies by Business World in the 
Consumer Services, Retail and Entertainment category.

Corporate Sustainability Assessment in the Textile, 
Apparel & Luxury category, earned the EcoVadis Silver 
Badge, maintained a 'Low Risk' rating from Sustainalytics 
for the Textile & Apparel industry, and reaffirmed our CDP 
Climate score of 'B', and improved our CDP Water score 
from 'B' to 'A-'.

robust governance, responsible business practices and 
disciplined execution will continue to strengthen our  
long-term competitiveness.

FY26 saw us deliver a resilient and sustainable value 
chain, backed by advanced technology and business 
management practices. We have deployed blockchain-
based supply chain tracker, an employee management 
system, and sustainable flooring solutions, holistically 
referred to as Welspun 2.0.
Our digital team embedded AI across the value chain 
to unlock new levels of productivity, precision, and 
performance that will help us transition from reactive 
operations to predictive and proactive decision-making, 
significantly improving efficiency. While this will enable us 
to live up to customer expectations, it will, in turn, enhance 
our reliability across businesses. 
The SAP S/4HANA technology created a unified digital 
backbone that brings together our manufacturing, retail, 
and global operations onto a single, agile platform. This 
transformation is strengthening our ability to make faster, 
data-driven decisions, enhance operational efficiency, 
and respond swiftly to evolving market demands.
As we expand our digital footprint, safeguarding our 
systems and data remains a top priority. We continuously 
strengthen our cyber security framework to ensure 
resilient, secure, and compliant operations across the 
enterprise. Our approach involves proactive monitoring, 
strong access control, data protection, and continuous 
risk assessment to mitigate cyber threats.
Led by value, locked in on 
customers
At the heart of this transformation lies a clear focus on 
value, while elevating customer experience through 
digital innovation. 
Our every initiative is anchored to improving efficiency, 
optimising working capital, enhancing quality, and 
driving sustainable growth. It empowers our teams with 
better tools, deeper insights, and a culture of continuous 
improvement, while it strengthens our customer-facing 
platforms to deliver seamless, intuitive, and responsive 
interactions across touchpoints.

response times, and enable personalised engagement 
with our customers, creating a differentiated experiences 
in a competitive global market.

Our Board convened 5 times in FY26 to deliberate 
on critical strategic and operational matters and 
consider macroeconomic developments and consumer 
sentiment to product innovation, cost optimisation, and 
digital transformation.
Backed by a robust offshore business, we are now looking 
inward to build on our domestic presence, where already 
we are one of the largest distributed home textile brands 
with an expanding retail presence. Riding on the digital 
wave, we are stressing on the direct-to-consumer (D2C) 
platforms and quick-commerce channels to address the 
evolving needs of consumers.

management, cyber security investments, and the refining 
enterprise-wide governance frameworks. We are not

enterprise that is resilient, intelligent, and ready to lead.

deliver excellence, innovation and long-term value.
The future we are creating today is not just digital — it 
is smarter, faster, safer, and has a deeper connect with 
our customers.

Economic review   
Global economy
The global economy entered a new phase in 2025, 
marked by the simultaneous pursuit of growth, 
resilience and strategic realignment. While global 
GDP grew by 3.4%1,  the operating environment was 
increasingly shaped by changing trade policies, 
geopolitical developments and the reconfiguration of 
global supply chains. Businesses across industries 
increasingly balanced efficiency with resilience 
as governments sought to strengthen economic 
security, diversify sourcing networks and recalibrate 
trade partnerships.
Against this backdrop, the most consequential 
development for export-oriented sectors was the 
emergence of a new global trade architecture. The 
escalation of US tariff measures and the acceleration 
of bilateral and regional trade negotiations signalled a 
structural reset in market access and competitiveness. 
For India, progress on trade agreements with key 
markets, including the United Kingdom and the 
European Union, alongside ongoing trade engagement 
with the United States, has the potential to redefine 
export opportunities and strengthen the country's 
position within global supply chains. 
Advanced economies: Moderation amid 
policy tightness
In the United States, resilient consumer spending drove 
growth to 2.0% in 2025, with a projected increase to 
2.4% in 2026. The US Dollar maintained its strength 
through safe-haven demand and divergent monetary 
policies. This lowered import costs for US consumers, 
tightened global liquidity and increased transaction 
costs for emerging markets. Meanwhile, the US labour 
market remained stable, with unemployment projected 
to hover around 4% through 2026.2 
Emerging markets: Sustained momentum
Emerging markets expanded by 4.4% in 2025 and are 
projected to stabilise at 4.2% and 4.1% in 2026 and 
2027, respectively, driven by resilient domestic demand 
and robust investment. In China, GDP grew by 5.0% 
in 2025 and is forecast at 4.5% for 2026, supported 
by manufacturing stimulus. However, escalating 
trade frictions and shifting tariff policies continue to 
complicate Chinese export dynamics, accelerating 
global supply chain diversification toward more stable 
manufacturing hubs.3
Inflation: Although easing remains above 
target levels 
Inflationary pressures showed signs of gradual 
moderation during the year. Global headline inflation is 
estimated at 4.1% in 2025 and projected to ease to 3.8% 
in 2026, supported by improving supply conditions and 
stabilising commodity prices.4	
 
However, inflation remains above target levels of 2%-
6% in several economies, prompting central banks to 
maintain relatively tight monetary policies. This has 
continued to influence global liquidity conditions and 
growth prospects.
In the US, easing tariff tensions with China and 
improvements in global supply chains have helped 
moderate inflation. Inflation is expected to decline to 
approximately 2.6% in 2026, while fading tariff effects 
and lower oil prices should bring core PCE inflation 
back to 2% during the first half of 2027.

Global cotton fundamentals: Production, 
demand and pricing
The global cotton market remained steady but subdued 
through the 2025–26 season, balancing an expanded 
agricultural output against a measured downstream 
consumption profile. According to the USDA, global 
cotton production is estimated at 121.9 million 
bales (nearly 26 million tonnes), reflecting a year-
on-year uptick driven by higher acreage, improving 
yields, and stable input conditions across primary 
producing nations like China, India, Brazil, and the US.6   
Conversely, global consumption is projected at a more 
moderate 119.1 million bales, resulting in a marginal 
production surplus that has built up global inventories 
and kept overall market pricing under pressure.7  
China and India continue to anchor global demand, 
collectively accounting for over half of global mill 
consumption. However, Chinese buying remained 
cautious due to ongoing trade frictions, slower export 
orders, and structural supply chain shifts. Reflecting 
these international linkages, the Indian domestic 
market experienced varied pricing across regional 
grades; according to the Cotton Association of India 
(CAI), upcountry spot prices for standard categories 
successfully stabilised between ₹54,000 and ₹60,600 
per candy in March 2026, depending on staple length 
and quality specifications.8  Moving forward, the 
global cotton matrix is expected to remain structurally 
sound and broadly stable, supported by a gradual 
normalisation of global trade flows and steady demand 
anchoring from the Indian and Chinese textile hubs.

Manufacturing push and policy support
The Government continued to prioritise large-scale 
manufacturing in FY26 through the Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) framework and the newly introduced 
Integrated Programme for the Textile Sector. Building 
on cumulative PLI-linked investments exceeding ₹1.61 
lakh crore in FY25,16 the Union Budget FY27 provided 
further impetus with 52 additional PLI approvals 
involving ₹6,708 crore in committed investments, 
specifically targeting Man-Made Fibre (MMF), 
technical textiles, and value-added manufacturing. 
This momentum was reinforced by new structural 
frameworks, including the National Fibre Scheme, 
the Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme, and 
the Tex-Eco Initiative, solidifying the state's focus on 
modernisation, sustainable manufacturing, and long-
term export competitiveness.
Exports and trade performance
India’s textile and apparel export ecosystem 
demonstrated strong resilience, expanding by 2.1% to 
reach ₹3,16,334.9 crore, up from ₹3,09,859.3 crore in 
the previous fiscal year.17 This expansion was achieved 
despite severe mid-year headwinds from the US 
reciprocal tariff regime, which temporarily squeezed 
traditional Western market channels before normalising 
early this year. Segment-wise, Ready-Made Garments 
(RMG) continued to anchor the export basket as the 
largest contributor, growing 2.9% to ₹1,39,349.6 crore, 
while Man-Made Fibre (MMF) textiles grew by 3.6% 
to ₹42,687.8 crore, reflecting a gradual and highly 
profitable market pivot toward specialised, technical, and 
synthetic lines.18 
Crucially for diversified manufacturers, this steady 
domestic export momentum was backed by aggressive 
geographic expansion, with growth recorded across 
more than 120 destinations, led by notable surges in 
the UAE (22.3%), Spain (15.5%), and the UK (7.8%).19 
This broad-based market footprint, paired with the 
structural extension of government support mechanisms 
such as the RoSCTL and RoDTEP schemes beyond 
March 2026, ensures a highly predictable regulatory 
and margin framework. This stability empowers scaled, 
vertically integrated market leaders to aggressively 
capture shifting global sourcing shares while insulating 
themselves from localised supply chain disruptions.
Trade policy developments: A structural reset 
FY26 marked a pivotal year for India’s textile and home textile sector, with a series of trade policy developments 
that have the potential to structurally reshape the country’s global competitive positioning. While the operating 
environment remained moderately challenging due to demand fluctuations and global uncertainties, these 
agreements signal a strong medium- to long-term opportunity for export-led growth.

The India-EU FTA negotiations have

•	 Category expansion: Beyond 
basic cotton sheets, zero-duty 
allows competitive entry into 
Technical Home Textiles (for

scaling: Elimination of duties

India-UK Free 
Trade Agreement
Effective 15 July 2026, the India–UK 
Comprehensive Economic and Trade 
Agreement (CETA) grants duty-free 
access to 99% of Indian exports to the 
UK, including textiles, apparel and home 
textiles, eliminating the 10–12% tariffs 
that previously applied to many of these 
products. The agreement significantly 
enhances the price competitiveness 
of Indian exporters in one of their key 
developed markets, creating opportunities 
for higher exports, greater investment and 
deeper integration into UK supply chains. 
Beyond tariff liberalisation, the FTA is 
expected to strengthen bilateral trade and 
investment, remove long-standing post-
Brexit trade barriers, and support the long-
term expansion of India's textile and apparel 
sector.22
•	 Levelling the playing field: India 
can finally match the Duty-free 
status enjoyed by Pakistan and 
Bangladesh. This is expected 
to trigger a volume surge in the 
textile categories.
•	 Design collaboration: The FTA 
encourages design houses in 
the UK to partner with Indian 
mills. This facilitates a shift from 
‘Contract Manufacturing’ (OEM) to 
‘Design-led Manufacturing’ (ODM), 
increasing the brand value of 
Indian exports.
•	 Retail partnership stability: 
Major UK retailers can now sign 
three- to five-year multi-billion-
dollar sourcing contracts with 
Indian mills without fearing sudden 
tariff hikes.

agreements enhancing market access and providing

navigate short-term fluctuations, while strengthening

Review of macroeconomic factors
The foreign exchange landscape
The Indian Rupee continued to reflect movements in 
global currency markets, with exchange rates at 93.50 
USD/INR, 109.00 EUR/INR and 125.63 GBP/INR in 
March 2026.24 
The continued depreciation of the Indian Rupee 
against major global currencies, has enhanced the 
price competitiveness of Indian exports in international 
markets. As the Rupee weakens, Indian goods become 
relatively more affordable for global buyers, US and 
Europe, thereby supporting export demand and 
potentially driving higher export volumes.
Dynamics of India’s cotton economy
Cotton is an essential commercial crop in India, 
accounting for approximately 24% of global cotton 
production and supporting the livelihoods of millions 
of farmers and workers. It significantly contributes to 
India's foreign exchange earnings through exports of 
raw cotton, intermediate products and finished goods.
India holds the largest cotton acreage globally, with 
114.47 lakh hectares under cultivation, accounting 
for nearly 37% of the world’s total cotton area. As the 
world’s second-largest producer and consumer of 
cotton, the country's estimated production of 294.25 
lakh bales (5.00 million metric tonnes) during the 2024-
25 season, representing approximately 20% of global 
output.25  Notably, India is the only nation that grows 
all four species of cotton: G. Arboreum & G. Herbaceum 
(Asian cotton), G. Barbadense (Egyptian cotton) and G. 
Hirsutum (American Upland cotton).26
Indian cotton prices showed moderate volatility during 
the year, broadly aligning with global trends. By March 
2026, Indian cotton maintained a stable position, with 
upcountry spot prices for standard grades ranging 
between approximately ₹155 and ₹180 per kg reflecting 
both domestic demand and global price linkages.27  
During the same period, international cotton prices 
remained relatively soft averaging approximately 61–66 
cents per pound in March 2026, compared to around 
63–68 cents per pound in March 2025, indicating a 
marginal softening in prices year-on-year amid ample 
global supply and subdued demand.28

Global textile and apparel trade
Global textile and apparel trade, estimated at 
approximately $900 billion in 2025, underwent its most 
significant structural disruption in decades during FY26. 
The escalation of US tariffs on Indian textiles to 50%, 
followed by the India-US trade reset and landmark 
trade agreements with EU and UK FTA to provide zero-
duty access, has triggered a fundamental realignment 
of global sourcing patterns. India, the world’s 
largest cotton producer and a vertically integrated 
manufacturing powerhouse, is emerging as the primary 
beneficiary of this ‘China Plus One’ acceleration.

As the world’s largest cotton producer, India stands 
out as a completely vertically integrated manufacturing 
powerhouse. Controlling the value chain from raw fibre 
to finished product allows India to serve as the primary 
strategic beneficiary of global vendor migration.

approximately 60% in 2025.

industrial manufacturing focus, directly 
supporting organised textile enterprises through 
targeted fiscal allocations and scale-driven

incentives for sustainable manufacturing,

budget continues to accelerate the rollout of 
seven PM MITRA (Mega Integrated Textile Region 
and Apparel) Parks, backed by an approved 
₹4,445 crore central investment through FY28. 
Designed to attract cumulative capital inflows of 
₹27,434 crore, this mega-infrastructure model 
lowers logistics friction, establishes world-class 
manufacturing clusters, and provides structured 
cost efficiencies that bolster the global 
competitiveness of large-scale exporters.

making it the single largest sourcing origin for these 
categories.48 
Looking ahead, this structural dominance is positioned 
to strengthen further. The progressive normalisation of 
trade terms, paired with the imminent operationalisation 
of milestone bilateral trade pacts, headlined by the 
India-UK and India-EU Free Trade agreement (FTA), 
presents a highly lucrative growth runway, unlocking 
duty-free market access to high-potential European 
zones. Over the long term, the Indian home textile 
ecosystem is projected to expand at a robust 8.9% 
CAGR, scaling from a baseline valuation of $10.78 
billion in 2023 to reach $23.32 billion by 2032, 
driven by institutional global vendor diversification 
and a permanent consumer preference shift toward 
innovative, sustainable, and traceable premium textile 
solutions.49

Regional Insights
The global flooring industry in 2025 continued to 
evolve around sustainable materials, resilient supply 
chains, and localised manufacturing, even as growth 
moderated across certain geographies. 
Regional demand profiles shifted significantly: North 
America’s market was heavily sustained by home 
renovation and remodelling activity, with US home 
improvement spending exceeding $400 billion, as 
elevated mortgage rates temporarily disincentivised 
new housing construction.56 In Europe, growth was 
primarily driven by strict sustainability mandates and 
regulatory frameworks like the Renovation Wave, which 
accelerated the adoption of low-emission, recyclable, 
and energy-efficient materials.57 Conversely, the Asia-
Pacific region remains the largest and fastest-growing

Indian flooring industry
The floor covering market in India was valued at $85.15 
million in 2025 and is projected to grow to $101.28 
million by 2030 at a CAGR of 3.53%.60 This expansion 
will be largely driven by the broader construction boom, 
which is expected to reach a market value of $1.4 
trillion by 2030.61 
The market is witnessing a shift towards high-quality, 
durable and low-maintenance solutions as project 
timelines tighten and cost-efficiency becomes critical. 
Beyond residential use, infrastructure development 
is emerging as a major catalyst; for instance, the 
expansion of the metro rail network with over 1,000 km 
of track (currently operational or under construction)
has created a massive demand for heavy-duty, slip-
resistant flooring at stations.62 Consequently, there 
is a surge in preference for materials that offer high 
wear resistance and hygiene, aligning with modern 
commercial and public infrastructure standards.

Company review 
Welspun Living Limited is a part of the Welspun world, 
one of India’s fastest-growing global conglomerates 
with diversified businesses spanning line pipes, home 
textile products, infrastructure, warehousing, steel, 
oil & gas, advanced textiles and flooring solutions. 
The Company is a global leader in home textiles and 
offers a wide range of products across bed, bath, 
rugs, advanced textiles and flooring categories. With 
a presence in over 60+ countries and manufacturing 
hubs in Anjar, Vapi, Telangana, and Ohio and Nevada 
US, the Company leverages a three-pronged approach 
anchored in innovation, sustainability and customer-
centricity to deliver top-tier, differentiated products. 
Our success is powered by a competent team 
comprising around 24,000 employees worldwide, 
extensive consumer research, vertically integrated 
facilities and strong partnerships with major global 
retailers. For over 36 years, the Company has sustained 
its position as India’s largest exporter of home textiles 
and the leading supplier to the US market. Its brand 
portfolio features cherished heritage names such as 
Christy, Welhome along with Indian power brands 
including Welspun and Spaces.
Guided by its core values of Learning, Innovation, Trust 
and Endurance, Welspun remains focused on creating 
smarter, more sustainable living spaces worldwide.

Key business and operational highlights
FY26 was a year shaped by global trade disruptions, 
tariff uncertainties, geopolitical tensions, and evolving 
consumer demand. Despite these external headwinds, 
Welspun Living demonstrated resilience through 
disciplined execution, strong customer partnerships, 
operational agility and strategic diversification.
Consolidated revenues for FY26 stood at ₹9,468 
crore, while EBITDA margins for the year stood at 9.1%. 
The Company remained focused on protecting long-
term customer relationships, strengthening operating 
efficiencies, and preserving financial discipline 
through a challenging cycle. Focused working capital 
optimisation and prudent capital allocation led to strong 
free cash flow generation and a sharp reduction in net 
debt during the year.
Management actions through FY26 remained deliberate 
and forward-looking. The Company accelerated 
geographic diversification, with the non-US business 
contribution expanding to ~41%, while continuing to 
invest in innovation, sustainability, branded businesses, 
and nearshore manufacturing capabilities. The year also 
marked the commencement of commercial production 
at Welspun Living’s Nevada greenfield pillow facility 
in the US, strengthening its long-term presence in the 
global sleep ecosystem.
India’s strengthening position as a preferred sourcing 
destination, supported by evolving trade frameworks 
with the US, UK, EU, Japan, and Australia, is creating 
significant long-term opportunities for the textile sector. 
Against this backdrop, Welspun Living’s diversified 
portfolio, branded offerings, integrated supply chain 
capabilities, innovation platforms, and sustainability 
leadership continue to strengthen its position as a 
preferred partner for leading global retailers.
The domestic consumer business remained a key 
growth driver during the year, with revenues growing 
~9% YoY, supported by stronger brand traction, 
premiumisation, and channel diversification. The 
Company’s global brands, including Christy and 
Welhome, continued to deepen presence across 
international markets, while sustainability leadership 
was reinforced through Welspun Living being ranked 
#1 globally in the 2025 S&P Global Corporate 
Sustainability Assessment for the Textile, Apparel & 
Luxury Goods category.
Backed by strong customer relationships, sustainability-
led operations, and disciplined execution, Welspun 
Living enters FY27 with a strengthened balance 
sheet, improving market positioning, and confidence 
in its ability to capture the next phase of growth 
opportunities globally.

ESG
Welspun Living has embedded Environmental, Social, 
and Governance (ESG) principles into its strategic 
decision-making framework since inception. This 
commitment, driven from the highest levels of 
leadership, has been validated by becoming #1 globally 
in ESG S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment in 
Textiles, Apparels & Luxury Goods category (as on  
December 11 2025).
Our Vision 2030 is anchored on achieving environment-
positive operations and meaningful community 
upliftment. We are generating renewable energy 
through onsite solar plants and procuring renewable 
energy through power purchase agreements (PPAs) 
wherever land is a constraint. Our advanced water and 
wastewater treatment facilities recycle more than half 
of our total water intake.
On the social front, our programmes span child 
education, women's empowerment, and sustainable 
agricultural training. Guided by robust governance 
frameworks and a culture of integrity, Welspun Living 
upholds transparent and ethical practices as the 
bedrock of sustainable, long-term growth. Our policies 
on ESG, Sustainable Sourcing, and Supplier Code of 
Conduct span our value chain and build a future-ready 
value chain.
ESG milestones in FY26
Environmental impacts
•	 Our renewable energy portfolio expanded to 60 MW 
across four facilities, supported by floating solar, 
rooftop solar, ground-mounted solar installations 
and renewable PPAs.
•	 Through design optimisation, equipment upgrades 
and process efficiency improvements, we achieved 
energy savings of over 8 million kWh, avoiding 
more than 10,800 tCO₂e emissions from energy 
conservation and an additional 17,000+ tCO₂e 
through the transition from fossil fuels to renewable 
energy sources.
•	 Our flagship facility at Anjar is on the path to 
achieve zero Scope 2 electricity-based emissions 
in the near future through one of our largest 
RERTC project.
•	 Recycled 3.6 billion litres of water during the 
reporting year, with recycled water accounting for 
59% of total water consumption.
•	 Diverted 99.7% of waste from landfill through 
responsible utilisation pathways, including the 
use of ETP sludge in boilers and co-processing of 
hazardous waste through authorised partners.
•	 Cotton being our primary raw material, 
sustainable cotton sourcing increased to 95%, 
advancing our journey towards our goal of 100% 
sustainable cotton.
•	 Increased sustainable packaging adoption to 83% 
through the use of 100% recycled cardboard and 
FSC-certified materials, reducing the environmental 
footprint of our packaging solutions.

Outlook 
Welspun Living enters FY27 with a clear strategic 
focus on advancing its sustainability agenda while 
delivering operational excellence and long-term 
stakeholder value.
The Company will continue to accelerate its renewable 
energy transition, supported by investments in solar 
energy, biomass-based solutions and waste heat 
recovery systems across its manufacturing facilities. 
These initiatives will further strengthen WLL’s pathway 
towards achieving 100% renewable energy by 2030.
WLL will deepen its integration of AI-driven ESG 
data platforms and blockchain-enabled supply chain 
systems to enhance real-time ESG monitoring and 
end-to-end traceability. The rollout of Digital Product 
Passports (DPPs) and Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs) 
across all product lines will ensure compliance with 
evolving global regulatory requirements and consumer 
sustainability standards.
The Company will continue to scale its sustainable 
cotton farming programme by onboarding additional 
farmers and advancing certified, traceable raw material 
sourcing practices across the value chain.
With a well-defined roadmap aligned to global ESG 
priorities, WLL remains well positioned to deliver 
resilient growth, strengthen stakeholder trust 
and create long-term value through purposeful 
sustainability leadership.

US tariffs and  
market concentration
Multiple FTAs with the European Union, UK and New Zealand are expected to effectively mitigate 
risks arising from tariff-impacted geographies. We are also working to deepen our presence by 
developing partnerships across new markets such as Australia, New Zealand, GCC countries and 
Japan. In addition, we continue to diversify our channels across Retail, Hospitality and E-commerce, 
while expanding into new product categories and strengthening our portfolio of licenced and owned 
brands.
Geopolitical uncertainty
We continue to diversify our market presence to reduce dependence on any single geography. Our 
expansion plans are focused on Europe, the UK, Japan and the wider APAC region. We maintain 
long-term contracts with suppliers and adequate cotton coverage of more than 4–5 months to 
support supply continuity. Management closely monitors evolving geopolitical developments and 
takes necessary steps to ensure uninterrupted availability of raw materials.
Major raw materials 
availability and pricing 
(Cotton/Fabric/Yarn)
Procurement plans are prepared well in advance, and we maintain adequate cotton coverage of 
approximately 4–5 months. Global cotton market developments are monitored through a structured 
review process supported by active coordination with the marketing team and various market 
intelligence tools. Safety stock levels have been reassessed to address higher lead times for 
imported cotton. We continue to increase the use of recycled cotton to optimise production costs 
while advancing sustainability objectives. Recycled cotton usage has increased to 20% over the last 
year compared to less than 15% previously. In addition, we have installed a cotton fibre recycling 
plant with a capacity of 4–5 tonnes per day at Anjar, which is now operational.
Exposure to volatility in 
foreign exchange rates
We have a robust foreign exchange policy in place to manage currency volatility, supported by 
continuous monitoring and periodic adjustment of hedge positions to facilitate timely corrective 
action.
Risk arising from 
inadequate 
attraction and retention of 
talent
We continue to invest in upskilling initiatives to enhance productivity and workforce capability, while 
implementing focused measures to attract, develop and retain skilled talent. Succession plans have 
also been established for all critical management positions.
ESG-related risks
A Board-level ESG and CSR Committee has been constituted to oversee, monitor and drive ESG and 
CSR initiatives across the organisation. We continue to implement our Board-approved roadmap 
towards carbon neutrality and remain focused on achieving 100% renewable energy by 2030, 
freshwater positivity by 2030, zero waste to landfill by 2027, 100% sustainable cotton sourcing by 
2030 and enhanced biodiversity outcomes.

growth in a competitive 
domestic and global 
environment
We consistently drive innovation to strengthen our competitive position and have diversified our 
business through Direct-to-Customer channels, alongside a stronger focus on the Indian domestic 
market. Expansion into adjacent businesses such as Advanced Textiles and Flooring has further 
supported risk diversification and sustainable business growth.

Executive Summary of report on Impact Assessment 
of CSR Project (Assessment was carried out by 
Protiviti)
 
A. 
Executive Summary
 
 
Protiviti conducted the impact assessment for 
eight CSR projects for FY 2024-25, covering 
WelKrishi, Welspun Super Sports Women, 
WelNetrutva, WelPrakruti, WelShiksha, 
WelSuraksha, WelSwasthya and WelDisha. 
The evaluation covered 1,002 intervention 
beneficiaries and 325 control or non-
beneficiaries wherever applicable, and was 
conducted at a significance level of 90% 
confidence and 5% margin of error. In addition 
to primary beneficiaries, other key stakeholders 
were also interviewed to strengthen the 
assessment and triangulate findings.
 
 
The evaluation was structured around the IRECS 
framework, which assessed Inclusiveness, 
Relevance, Effectiveness, Convergence and 
Sustainability. The assessment focused on 
understanding the extent to which desired 
outcomes and impacts were achieved, whether 
project outputs were effectively and efficiently 
delivered by implementation teams, the potential 
risks and opportunities in each project, and the 
success stories and recommendations that can 
inform future programming.
 
 
A qualitative approach was used for drawing 
inferences on outcomes and impact among target 
beneficiaries. The evaluation tools included 
Key Informant’s Interview Questionnaire, Fixed 
Group Discussion and Observation checklists.

The combination of beneficiary consultations, 
control group comparisons wherever applicable 
and stakeholder interviews provided a broad 
evidence base for understanding both immediate 
outputs and visible changes generated through 
the CSR projects.
 
 
Across thematic areas, the CSR program 
demonstrated visible improvements in 
education, healthcare, road safety, livelihoods, 
agriculture, environment, women’s sports and 
skill development. The education interventions 
contributed to improved learning outcomes, 
digital skills, career awareness, classroom 
participation and athlete support. The healthcare 
interventions improved health awareness, 
access to care, health-seeking behaviour, 
nutritional intake and reduced out-of-pocket 
expenditure. Road safety interventions improved 
awareness, emergency response readiness, 
understanding of the Good Samaritan Law 
and healthcare access for drivers. Livelihood 
interventions strengthened employable skills, 
income generation, enterprise creation, women’s 
financial decision-making and farm productivity. 
Agriculture and environment interventions 
contributed to better yield bands, soil health, 
water-use efficiency, reduced stalk burning, 
expanded green cover, water storage capacity, 
community ownership and environmental 
awareness. The women empowerment and skill 
development interventions supported athletes’ 
performance, rankings, resilient comebacks, 
job readiness, confidence, placement-linked 
training and early income generation among 
placed beneficiaries.
 
B. 
Scope of work and Evaluation Coverage
 
 
The scope of work covered eight CSR projects 
for FY 2025-26. WelNetrutva covered 210 
intervention beneficiaries and 80 control 
beneficiaries across Telangana, Gujarat, Uttar 
Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. WelSwasthya 
covered 160 intervention beneficiaries and 80 
control beneficiaries across Telangana, Gujarat, 
Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. WelShiksha 
covered 180 intervention beneficiaries and 80 
control beneficiaries across Telangana, Gujarat 
and Madhya Pradesh. WelKrishi covered 178 
intervention beneficiaries and 85 control 
beneficiaries across Gujarat and Maharashtra.
 
 
The evaluation also covered WelDisha with 
40 intervention beneficiaries in Telangana, 
WelSuraksha with 100 intervention beneficiaries 
across Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, 
WelPrakruti with 100 intervention beneficiaries 
across Telangana, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, 
and Welspun Super Sports Women with 34 
intervention beneficiaries across pan-India 
locations. Overall, the evaluation reached 1,002 
intervention beneficiaries and 325 control or 
non-beneficiary respondents. Other relevant 
stakeholders were also interviewed to provide 
additional context on implementation, outcomes 
and future opportunities.
 
C. 
Evaluation Framework and Methodology
 
 
The IRECS framework was used as the evaluation 
lens. Inclusiveness assessed the extent to 
which the projects ensured that vulnerable 
stakeholders equitably benefitted from 
interventions. Relevance assessed whether 
project interventions were equipped to address 
the priority needs of targeted stakeholders. 
Effectiveness assessed the extent to which 
desired project outcomes were achieved by 
making the best possible use of available 
resources. Convergence assessed the extent 
to which projects collaborated with external 
stakeholders and leveraged resources for project 
outputs and outcomes. Sustainability assessed 
whether the benefits of the projects continued or 
were likely to continue after project exit.
 
 
The evaluation objectives were to assess 
achievement of desired outcomes and impact, 
examine whether outputs were delivered 
effectively and efficiently by implementation 
teams, identify potential risks and opportunities 
across the projects, and document success 
stories and recommendations for future 
programming. The evaluation adopted a 
qualitative approach for drawing inferences on 
outcomes and impact on target beneficiaries, 
supported by Key Informant’s Interview 
Questionnaire, Fixed Group Discussion and 
Observation checklists. The sample included 
1,002 intervention respondents and 325 control 
respondents, with significance set at 90% 
confidence and 5% margin of error.

Domain Wise Evaluation Summary
	
	
a) 
Education – WelShiksha- WelShiksha 
focused on improving access to quality 
education and learning outcomes 
for children in government schools.  
The program implemented foundational 
literacy and numeracy interventions 
reaching 15,000+ students, remedial 
academic support through Mohalla Classes 
and Evening Tuition Centres for 2,800+ 
academically vulnerable students, and 
deployed 54 para-teachers to provide 
individualised academic support to more 
than 5,300 students. It also strengthened 
digital learning access and delivered career 
counselling, pre-vocational training, life 
skills training, science exhibitions, Bal

Sabha, summer camps, co-curricular

The program demonstrated improvement

students scoring approximately 216% 
higher than control students in English, 
88% higher in Mathematics and 113% 
higher in Science. It also contributed to 
higher levels of classroom participation, 
greater willingness among students to ask

b) 
Healthcare – WelSwasthya- WelSwasthya 
aimed to improve preventive and curative 
health outcomes for adolescent girls, 
women and the wider community. The 
program conducted preventive health 
awareness sessions on nutrition, hygiene, 
menstrual health, maternal care and RTIs/
STIs for 2,02,673 beneficiaries. It provided 
health camps and curative care services, 
including free consultations, diagnostics, 
medicines and referrals for 34,000+ 
beneficiaries. Mobile Medical Unit services 
delivered doorstep healthcare to 22,838 
beneficiaries in remote and hard-to-
reach locations, while anaemia screening, 
malnutrition screening, maternal health 
support and linkages to government health

The program improved awareness of 
health and hygiene practices, with the 
intervention population demonstrating 
two times higher knowledge on healthcare 
and hygiene compared to the control 
population. 75% of beneficiaries reported 
improved access to healthcare services 
due to health camps, screening services, 
MMUs, free medicines and referrals. 
Average annual healthcare spending was 
lower in intervention households at ₹1,860 
compared to ₹3,166 in control households, 
reflecting a reduction of approximately 41%. 
Health-seeking behaviour also improved, 
with 65% of the intervention population 
demonstrating willingness to seek medical 
care immediately after health challenges 
compared to 16% in the control group. The 
program also increased comfort among 
women and adolescent girls in discussing 
sensitive health issues, improved nutritional 
intake and contributed to a rise in average 
haemoglobin levels from 7.2 g/dL to 10.8 g/
dL among beneficiaries.
	
	
c) 
Road Safety – WelSuraksha- WelSuraksha 
addressed road safety and health 
challenges faced by drivers, students and 
the general public in high-traffic regions. 
The program conducted FM Radio-based 
road safety campaigns across intervention 
states, reaching 2,75,220 beneficiaries over 
13,143 square kilometres. It also delivered 
school and college road safety awareness 
sessions to 8,871 students, first aid and CPR 
training workshops for 2,755 beneficiaries, 
road safety rallies and public awareness 
drives for 2,120 community members, and 
road safety rath campaigns reaching 90,114 
beneficiaries along high-traffic highway 
corridors. Eye check-up camps and OPD, 
RTI/STI and general health camps were also 
conducted for commercial drivers and other 
target groups.
 
 
 
The program improved beneficiaries’ 
understanding of traffic rules, helmet and 
seatbelt usage, safe road-crossing practices 
and emergency response protocols. First 
aid and CPR training improved community 
capacity to respond during road accidents 
and medical emergencies. Beneficiaries 
also showed improved understanding of the 
Good Samaritan Law, reducing hesitation 
in assisting accident victims. Targeted 
health camps enabled early detection of 
TB, HIV, RTI/STI and eye conditions among 
commercial drivers, who are traditionally 
underserved. These changes indicate 
potential for reduced road accidents in the 
long run.
 
 
 
Going forward, the program should adopt a 
structured module and incremental learning 
approach by expanding the frequency of 
awareness sessions in schools and colleges, 
first aid workshops, radio initiatives and 
health screenings. Partnerships with

RTOs, traffic police and schools should be 
strengthened to integrate road safety into 
formal curricula and sustain safe road-
use practices.
	
	
d) 
Livelihood - WelNetrutva - Women 
Focused - The women-focused 
component of WelNetrutva aimed to 
empower women and community members 
by enhancing their skills and livelihood 
opportunities. It provided skill enhancement 
training in tailoring, macramé, weaving, 
food processing, beauty and wellness to 
650 individuals; enterprise development 
training and financial and technical support 
to 1,100 individuals; and SHG training to 
1,540 individuals.
 
 
 
The program contributed to employable 
skill acquisition, with 87% of intervention 
beneficiaries reporting employable skills 
compared to 42% in the control population. 
57% of intervention beneficiaries were 
consistently earning income through skills 
training and enterprise support, compared 
to 28% in the control population. 29% of 
intervention beneficiaries established 
micro-enterprises, compared to less 
than 5% in the control group. Intervention 
households earned 48% higher income 
than control households across states, 
with average annual income of ₹2,11,554 
among intervention households compared 
to ₹1,42,942 among control households. 
Women’s financial decision-making 
also improved, with 83% of women in 
intervention households reporting that 
they independently decided how to use 
their income, compared to 31% in control 
households. 85% of women beneficiaries 
reported improved self-confidence 
after enrolment.
 
 
 
Going forward, targeted efforts are required 
to strengthen market linkages and access 
to finance, particularly in regions such as 
Telangana where conversion from skill 
training to income has been limited. The 
program should select skill training trades 
based on market studies and demand 
assessments to improve relevance and 
effectiveness, either through empirical 
research or by leveraging existing 
studies, including those conducted by 
government departments.
	
	
e) 
Livelihood - WelNetrutva - Farmer 
Focused - The farmer-focused 
component of WelNetrutva supported 
agricultural livelihoods through guidance, 
demonstrations and on-field capacity-
building for 21,000+ farmers. It established 
a community seed bank benefiting 500+ 
farmers, supported brucellosis vaccination 
and tagging of 2,300 cattle, provided fodder 
input support to 241 farmers, IPM service 
support to 248 farmers, and set up a bio-
resource centre benefiting 710+ farmers 
through input support and trainings.
 
 
 
The program improved knowledge of 
modern farming and animal husbandry 
practices, with 95% of intervention 
farmers reporting moderate to significant 
improvement, compared to less than 20% 
of control farmers who had knowledge of 
modern practices. All intervention farmers 
had access to input support, seed bank 
facilities, vaccination support, cattle health 
camps and IPM services, while no such 
services were available to control farmers. 
Intervention farmers reported an average 
33% improvement in yield, 31% reduction 
in input costs, 45% reduction in chemical 
fertiliser and pesticide use, and 22% 
reduction in crop loss. Vaccination and 
health camps contributed to more than 20% 
reduction in disease and mortality among 
cattle. Intervention farmers also reported 
61% higher farm income than control 
farmers, with average annual income of 
₹2,44,610 compared to ₹1,58,177 among 
control farmers.
 
 
 
Going forward, the program should consider 
expansion into nearby underserved regions, 
as there is strong unmet demand for 
program services among non-beneficiaries. 
This would increase outreach and improve 
overall program reach.
	
	
f) 
Agriculture – WelKrishi- WelKrishi 
promoted sustainable cotton farming, 
farmer livelihoods and environmental 
resilience through the adoption of Better 
Cotton Initiative principles, organic 
farming practices and capacity-building 
interventions. The program engaged 13,056 
cotton farmers in Gujarat and Maharashtra, 
targeted 1,439 women farmers, facilitated 
and supported 221 farmer learning groups, 
and enabled procurement of 32,387 
cotton bales in Gujarat and Maharashtra. 
It conducted 1,684 soil sample tests and 
2,659 demonstrations covering seed 
treatment, biofertilizer, farmer field schools 
and high-density planting trials. It also 
conducted 1,174 trainings, supported 417 
farmers in livelihood improvement activities, 
supported approximately 1,000 households 
through kitchen gardens, enabled 2,170 
farmers to adopt drip and sprinkler irrigation

in adopting home-made botanicals for 
plant protection.
 
 
 
The evaluation found that yield performance 
of BCI intervention farmers was largely 
concentrated in the mid to higher yield bands, 
particularly in Wardha and Aurangabad, 
with a higher proportion of intervention 
farmers reporting yields above 6 quintals 
per acre compared to control farmers. 
Beneficiaries reported improvements in soil 
health parameters such as fertility, moisture, 
texture and reduced erosion. Intervention 
farmers reported an average 12% reduction 
in water use compared to control farmers. 
Burning of cotton stalks has practically 
disappeared in Wardha and Aurangabad and 
was limited to 11% in Kutch, representing 
a considerable gain in terms of reducing 
carbon footprint. WelKrishi-supported 
farmers, both BCI and organic, showed 
a consistent positive shift toward higher
